parallel.requirements: Recognized the JWT HS256 port, required manual argv parsing, ESM .mjs modules, /output placement, zero external dependencies, and no node:crypto use.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent observed executable behavior, delegated sha256/hmac, base64url/jsonutil, and pyrepr/argparse to three children, and kept jwt.mjs plus test10.mjs integration for itself.
parallel.implementation: Children wrote the lower-level libraries; after their completed reports, the parent wrote jwt.mjs using hmac/base64/jsonutil and test10.mjs using argparse and pyrepr.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: All child reports returned through AgentSwarm, the parent wrote the integrated entrypoint, read output files for final reporting, and artifact validation later found the expected entry plus library files.
parallel.verification: Parent and children ran node checks, sample comparisons, Unicode/escape cases, and error-path checks; local output was reported as matching, but official evaluation later passed only 31/70.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No child was cancelled or left unjoined; the remaining defect was an unresolved hidden-case behavior shared with the serial solution, not a visible parallel coordination failure.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same JWT HS256, argparse, ESM, /output, zero-dependency, no node:crypto, and black-box executable-observation requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Single main agent owned observation, all library implementation, entrypoint assembly, debugging, verification, and final response without delegation.
serial.implementation: The serial agent wrote sha256, hmac, base64url, pyjson, jwt, argparse, and test10.mjs, then patched pyjson/jwt after detecting a compact payload serialization mismatch.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Because all work was local, imports and entrypoint assembly were controlled by one actor; artifact validation later found test10.mjs and the expected library files.
serial.verification: Serial ran executable probes, a direct node run that exposed token mismatch, a broader comparison with program-name mismatches, and a normalized final check that passed locally, while official evaluation passed 31/70.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial final response reported local success, but hidden official tests still failed at the same 31/70 rate as the parallel run; the exact hidden defect is not localized by the mounted evidence.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel identified the full migration target: JWT HS256 encode/decode, argparse-compatible CLI, ESM .mjs files, no external packages, no node:crypto, and /output delivery.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial received and acted on the same prompt requirements for the identical task, agent, and prompt hash.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference is evidenced; both failures occurred after apparently similar requirement coverage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed into three child-owned module groups while the parent retained jwt.mjs, test10.mjs, integration, and final verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all implementation and verification in one main-agent plan, writing every module itself.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced handoffs but assigned clear ownership; serial avoided handoffs by using one owner for the whole implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Child briefs specified file paths, exports, import suffixes, verification duties, and non-overlapping scopes; the aggregate handoff returned each child result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no cross-agent interface; it maintained the component contracts internally while creating and patching modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel required explicit module contracts, but no missing or conflicting contract materialized; serial's local ownership made the interface boundary simpler.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child modules implemented hashing, HMAC, base64url, JSON serialization, repr, and argparse; the parent then wrote JWT and entrypoint files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the same functional stack locally and then patched payload serialization after observing a mismatch.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The main concrete implementation difference was organization and naming, not a known divergent algorithm that explains the official score.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All three child results completed and returned through AgentSwarm before the parent began final integration.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; the main agent carried local findings directly into later edits.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a join point, but no result was missing, late, trapped, or ignored; serial avoided that lifecycle entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used shared /output but with separated file scopes, then parent-owned jwt.mjs and test10.mjs assembly and read back final files for reporting.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote and edited all files itself, including pyjson.mjs and jwt.mjs corrections, before final reporting.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel shared-state risk did not materialize as a collision or overwrite; serial's single-writer path was simpler but produced the same official failure rate.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified sample cases, Unicode/escape/astral cases, and argparse error paths locally, then declared completion, but official evaluation passed 31/70.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verified sample and edge cases locally, found and fixed compact JSON output, normalized program-name-only error differences, then official evaluation also passed 31/70.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both relied on local black-box comparisons that missed hidden evaluator cases; this is shared verification insufficiency rather than a parallel-only coordination failure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used 456.5 agent seconds and three subagents, completed without timeout, and closed after local verification and final response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used 317.372 agent seconds, no subagents, completed without timeout, and closed after local verification and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel cost more time and tokens, but there is no evidence that budget pressure displaced required work or caused the shared official failure.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The outcome is both_fail, not discordant: both completed official evaluations report 31 passed samples out of 70 and solution_passed false. Parallel's decomposition into child modules changed the workflow shape but all children returned and were integrated before local verification. Serial solved the same implementation locally and reached the same official score, so the evidence supports a shared hidden implementation or acceptance gap rather than a parallel-specific adverse coordination pattern.
parallel_contributors: Three child modules plus parent-owned JWT and entrypoint were completed and locally verified before final response.
Local comparisons covered visible sample, Unicode, escape, astral, and CLI error behavior but still did not expose the hidden official failures.
serial_contributors: Single-agent implementation found and patched compact JSON serialization before final local verification.
Normalized local checks passed, yet the completed official evaluation matched the same 31/70 failure rate.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used separate jsonutil.mjs and pyrepr.mjs modules from child handoffs; serial combined JSON and repr behavior in pyjson.mjs.
Parallel child agent-1 used python3 as a JSON oracle during its own verification despite the original task's executable-only instruction, but no artifact or outcome consequence is evidenced.
Serial initially emitted a token with payload JSON spaces, detected the mismatch, and patched pyjson/jwt to compact payload serialization.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; shared official failure with no retained parallel coordination pattern

candidates.reason: Parallel assigned implementation ownership for sha256/hmac, base64/json serialization, pyrepr/argparse, and parent-owned jwt/entrypoint work; implementation was not ownerless.
The parent explicitly retained integration ownership, joined child module reports, and wrote jwt.mjs and test10.mjs using the returned modules.
The final entrypoint and deliverable placement were parent-owned and completed; artifact validation lists test10.mjs as the expected entry.
The parent covered observation, delegation, join, integration, local verification, and final response, so no end-to-end transition was unowned.
The parent did initial executable probes before delegation, but productive child implementation then proceeded and no required implementation stage was blocked behind a harmful preflight gate.
Investigation did not remain a separate first phase performed by investigators only; after brief probing, implementation work was delegated and completed.
The indispensable parent integration path started after all child module reports and completed with local verification; no auxiliary allocation starved it.
The fan-out was three children, all completed, the parent continued integration, and the run did not time out or exhaust the official budget before closure.
Each child scope was bounded to a small module group and returned completed files plus tests; no single overbroad child left indispensable work unfinished.
Child briefs included file scope, ESM suffix/import rules, zero dependencies, no node:crypto, and concrete verification expectations; no child output became unusable from a missing known requirement.
The parallel split gave explicit exported function names and import paths for separately owned modules, and the parent assembled them without observed interface incompatibility.
No known finding disappeared during transfer; child reports returned file names, signatures, caveats, and verification results that the parent could consume.
The AgentSwarm aggregate was long but structured by child and was immediately followed by parent integration, so it was not materially unconsumed.
No returned child report described a superseded workspace state that the parent then used; integration followed the completed child reports.
The returned child contracts were compatible; agent-1's escaping caveat did not conflict with another handoff or block parent integration.

The parent did make a completion statement after local checks, but there was no non-evaluator evidence of a parent-visible unresolved integrated mismatch before closure; hidden official failures alone do not qualify.
There was no replacement child or repeated delegation without inherited findings; child self-tests and serial edits carried forward their observed state.

candidates.reason: All three child agents reached completed handoffs; no active child was cancelled or stopped before needed work was finalized.
The parent promoted child modules into jwt.mjs and test10.mjs before final local verification; no complete candidate remained unplaced at closure.
The parent performed integration writes before its final sample and edge-case verification, not after the relevant verification pass.
The AgentSwarm result returned all three implementation reports and the parent proceeded to write the dependent JWT and entry files using them.
Verification findings were included in the returned child reports; no separate verifier result was trapped below the parent.
No required child failed, aborted, or was cancelled; child-level test failures were resolved inside the same child trajectory before handoff.
The parent did not ignore an available child result; it consumed the completed swarm output and then wrote dependent integration files.
The parent did not wait until timeout or a decision deadline; it joined completed children and continued with integration and tests.
Parallel file scopes were separated by function and no competing cross-file design required unplanned reconciliation.
No two live agents edited the same source file, and no same-file reconciliation was observed.
No non-entry library source produced by one actor was replaced or wholesale rewritten by another actor.
The parent alone wrote the entrypoint test10.mjs; no other live actor owned or replaced that deliverable.
There was no cleanup, rebuild, or promotion step replacing multiple final outputs or invalidating another actor's final-tree work.
Although children wrote into /output, their assigned files were isolated and no unstable shared-state or provenance problem materialized.
No generated cache, fixture, temporary file, or auxiliary artifact from one concurrent actor was consumed by another as an unintended reference environment.

cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were reviewed; no observed child, handoff, lifecycle, wait, write, or acceptance episode cleared the retention gate.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: The run used parallelism, but all children completed and were joined; shared official failure alone was not converted into a concurrency label.
